steps.title: Welcome!
steps.purpose: Greet the child and set emotional tone
steps.owlText: Hello friend! Today we are going to practice everything we know about fractions! We will identify halves and quarters, find equal parts, and share fairly. Ready?
steps.studentText: Today we practice everything about fractions: halves, quarters, equal parts, and fair sharing!

media.altText: Owl teacher waving hello with various fraction shapes: halves, quarters, equal parts
media.fallbackText: Owl teacher waving hello with various fraction shapes: halves, quarters, equal parts

steps.title: Our Mission
steps.purpose: Tell the child what they will learn
steps.studentText: Today you will practice identifying halves and quarters, finding equal parts, and solving fair sharing problems. It is a fractions workout!

steps.title: Think First!
steps.purpose: Activate prior knowledge about all fraction concepts
steps.owlText: Before we start, think about this: What do you remember about fractions? What is a half? What is a quarter? What does 'equal parts' mean? Think about everything you know!
steps.studentText: What do you remember about fractions? What is a half? What is a quarter? What are equal parts?

media.altText: A mind-map style image with 'fractions' in the center and branches: half, quarter, equal parts, sharing
media.fallbackText: A mind-map style image with 'fractions' in the center and branches: half, quarter, equal parts, sharing

interaction.question: What do you remember about fractions? Tell me about halves, quarters, and equal parts.

steps.title: Learn It
steps.owlText: Let us review everything! A half (1/2) is one of two equal parts. A quarter (1/4) is one of four equal parts. Fractions need equal parts — the parts must be the same size. When you share fairly, everyone gets the same amount. Let us practice all of these!
steps.studentText: Review: One half (1/2) = one of two equal parts. One quarter (1/4) = one of four equal parts. Fractions need equal parts. Fair sharing means everyone gets the same amount.

media.altText: Four panels: (1) rectangle 2 parts 1 shaded = 1/2, (2) rectangle 4 parts 1 shaded = 1/4, (3) equal vs unequal comparison, (4) 2 children sharing 1 chapati equally
media.caption: All fraction concepts: halves, quarters, equal parts, fair sharing.
media.fallbackText: Four panels: (1) rectangle 2 parts 1 shaded = 1/2, (2) rectangle 4 parts 1 shaded = 1/4, (3) equal vs unequal comparison, (4) 2 children sharing 1 chapati equally

steps.title: Real Life Connection
steps.purpose: Connect all fraction concepts to real life
steps.owlText: Fractions are everywhere! When you cut a chapati in half, that is 1/2. When you cut a cake into 4 equal slices, each is 1/4. When you share food fairly, you are using fractions. When you fold paper evenly, you are making fractions. You use fractions every day!
steps.studentText: Fractions are everywhere: food, paper folding, sharing, shapes. Look for halves and quarters around you!

media.altText: Real life collage: chapati cut in half, cake in 4 slices, paper folded evenly, children sharing food
media.fallbackText: Real life collage: chapati cut in half, cake in 4 slices, paper folded evenly, children sharing food

steps.title: Watch and Learn
steps.purpose: Show worked examples of mixed fraction tasks
steps.owlText: Let me show you some examples. Example 1: This shape is divided into 2 equal parts. One is shaded. What fraction? One half (1/2)! Example 2: This shape is divided into 4 equal parts. One is shaded. What fraction? One quarter (1/4)! Example 3: 2 children share a chapati fairly. What fraction each? One half (1/2)!
steps.studentText: Practice identifying: Count the equal parts. 2 parts = 1/2. 4 parts = 1/4. Fair sharing: same number of people = same fraction each.

media.altText: Three worked examples: (1) 1/2 shape, (2) 1/4 shape, (3) fair sharing with 2 children. Each with answer shown.
media.fallbackText: Three worked examples: (1) 1/2 shape, (2) 1/4 shape, (3) fair sharing with 2 children. Each with answer shown.

steps.title: Your Turn!
steps.owlText: Now it is your turn! Look at this shape. It is divided into equal parts. One part is shaded. What fraction is shaded?
steps.studentText: This shape has one part shaded. How many equal parts is the whole divided into? What fraction is shaded?

media.altText: A rectangle divided into 2 equal parts with 1 part shaded.
media.fallbackText: A rectangle divided into 2 equal parts with 1 part shaded.

interaction.question: What fraction is shaded?
interaction.feedbackCorrect: Yes! The shape is divided into 2 equal parts and 1 is shaded. That is one half!
interaction.feedbackIncorrect: Count the total equal parts. There are 2. One is shaded. That is one half (1/2).

steps.title: Quick Check!
steps.owlText: Quick check! 2 children want to share a chapati fairly. What fraction does each child get?
steps.studentText: 2 children share one chapati fairly. What fraction does each child get?

media.altText: A chapati with 2 children beside it. The chapati is divided into 2 equal parts.
media.fallbackText: A chapati with 2 children beside it. The chapati is divided into 2 equal parts.

interaction.question: 2 children share one chapati fairly. What fraction does each child get?
interaction.feedbackCorrect: Correct! When 2 children share fairly, each gets one half. That is fair sharing!
interaction.feedbackIncorrect: If 2 children share one chapati fairly, we cut it into 2 equal parts. Each child gets 1 out of 2 parts. That is one half.

steps.title: Think About Your Learning
steps.owlText: You did great today! Think about what you learned. You practiced halves, quarters, equal parts, and fair sharing. You are becoming a fractions expert!
steps.studentText: What did you learn about fractions today?

interaction.question: How do you feel about fractions today?

steps.title: You Did It!
steps.owlText: Wonderful! You practiced all your fraction skills today. You can identify halves and quarters, find equal parts, and share fairly. Keep looking for fractions everywhere!
steps.studentText: You practiced fractions! You know halves, quarters, equal parts, and fair sharing!

media.altText: Celebration with stars and a badge that says 'I practiced fractions!'
media.fallbackText: Celebration with stars and a badge that says 'I practiced fractions!'
